sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section provides the header information for the maamar, including the Torah portion and date.

translations.translation: With the help of Heaven.
Shabbos Parshas Haazinu,
Shabbos Teshuvah,
the year 5737*

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section questions the redundancy of the verse, since "Return, O Israel" already implies verbal confession, and asks why "Take words with you" and "return to Hashem" are added.

translations.translation: "Return, O Israel, to Hashem your G-d... Take words with you and return to Hashem."1
And it needs to be understood,
that when it says "Return, O Israel," the intention is repentance as it should be,
and since it is a positive commandment to confess
(when one repents)2,
to the extent that confession is among the essentials of repentance3,
then "Return, O Israel" also includes verbal confession,
so what is added by "Take words with you"?4
Likewise, the continuation "and return to Hashem" must be explained,
for from this it is implied that after the repentance of "Return, O Israel,"
there needs to be yet another repentance.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains two interpretations of "until" in the verse: one referring to making Hashem your G-d, and another referring to a level above the chain of descent, with two sub-levels of "until."

translations.translation: And this will be understood by prefacing what was explained above5,
that what is written "Return, O Israel, until Hashem your G-d"
(even though ostensibly it should have said "to Hashem your G-d"),
is,
according to the explanation of the Alter Rebbe6,
that the repentance must be until Hashem becomes your G-d.
And there is another explanation7
regarding "Return, O Israel, until,"
that "until" refers to a level above that which is called "until"8.
And also in this there are two levels,
"until and including" and "until but not including."
"Until and including" is
(generally)
in the levels within the order of the chain of descent,
where all the levels in the chain of descent are relative to one another,
therefore,
even when one is in a lower level, he already has a connection to the levels above it,
and up to the highest level,
"until and including."
And "until but not including" is in that which is above the chain of descent,
for even when one is in the highest level within the chain of descent,
he will not thereby reach the level that is above the chain of descent,
"until but not including."
